A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on 65 unlearning models and nine jailbreaking models, including benchmark results, attack comparisons, and predictive analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The capability-suppression versus capability-elicitation framework and attack implementations remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same unlearning methods, universal attack adaptations, perturbations, pruning, and fine-tuning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same unlearning, utility, and jailbreaking coverage, including WMDP-Bio, MMLU, MT-Bench, AGIEval, the separate UK AISI biology evaluation, and Cascade attacks. V2's expanded data descriptions do not establish additional datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eight unlearning methods, nine jailbreaking models, and eleven standard attacks. The corresponding UK AISI and Cascade comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training data quantities, evaluation metrics, hyperparameters in Tables 3–5, and Appendix C cross-validation procedures are unchanged. V2's four-predictor numerical example refers to a configuration already evaluated in v1.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same PCA, clustering, attack-correlation, fine-tuning sensitivity, cross-task residual, and worst-case versus average-case prediction analyses. Figure 13's additional interpretation is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Weighted correlations, displayed p values and their non-i.i.d. caveat, cross-validation averaging, and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained. No repeated-run information or statistical estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables and plotted results are unchanged, but Section 4.1.3 replaces the three-predictor 0.77-to-0.82 example with 0.77-to-0.83 using four predictors. The latter matches Figure 13's values but incorrectly calls its R2 metric r. The expanded Figure 13 caption also newly reports a GCG–AutoPrompt correlation of 0.88, whereas Figure 12 shows 0.97.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the weighted PCA construction, the universal BEAST formulation, and Appendix C.1's modified R2 definition and reasoning remain unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions and central findings remain the same: benchmarking, low-dimensional robustness, predictive and conservative attack-success estimation, and the released model suite. The open-weight threat emphasized in v2's abstract was already explicit in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: Figure 13's caption adds an argument that similarity among known input attacks may understate tampering attacks' predictive value against novel threats. The discussion emphasizes safety cases and replaces the larger-model/task future-work item with tampering robustness. Existing model-family and cross-task limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly specifies biology papers and prompt–response pairs as attack-data formats. It drops v1's explicit statement about averaging fine-tuning results across retain/forget datasets and its 64-example specification for non-fine-tuning jailbreaking attacks. Appendix A's hyperparameters and model-access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Clymer et al. on safety cases and connects its evaluation methodology more explicitly to The Elicitation Game. The Hofstätter citation is updated and used more extensively; the broader related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, method subheadings, attack-data bullet list, discussion, and captions. Terminology shifts toward conservative estimates and the renamed UK AI Security Institute, while the main section and appendix sequence remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The two-column main text and references become single-column, with redesigned author presentation, typography, and extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 2 moves from the introduction to the experiments; Figure 1's label and several captions and table headings change. All nineteen figures and six tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the threat models and data presentation and replaces v1's mismatched prediction example with values matching the four-predictor plot. However, it introduces the incorrect Figure 13 correlation, labels R2 as r, and omits explicit reproducibility details. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these clarity gains and reporting losses leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
